title: Napoleon Cannot Refuse Jenner
text:
In 1796 the English country doctor Edward Jenner showed that inoculation with cowpox could protect people against smallpox, one of the deadliest diseases of the age. Vaccination spread quickly across Europe, including France. Napoleon Bonaparte admired it and had his soldiers vaccinated.

When war between Britain and France resumed in 1803, Napoleon ordered the detention of British civilians who happened to be in France, and many British prisoners were held there for years. Their families appealed to Jenner, whose name was respected throughout Europe, and he wrote to the French authorities asking for the release of several of them.

According to Jenner's early biographer John Baron, one petition was presented to Napoleon, who was about to reject it. Then the Empress Josephine mentioned the name of the man who had signed it. Napoleon stopped and said, "Ah, Jenner, I can refuse nothing to that man." The prisoners were released. Jenner was able to secure the freedom of a number of British detainees this way, at a time when the two nations were at war.
lesson: Good done for everyone earns trust and goodwill even among opponents. A reputation for serving people beyond your own side can open doors that are closed to everyone else.
people: Edward Jenner, Napoleon Bonaparte, Josephine Bonaparte
source: John Baron, The Life of Edward Jenner (1827 to 1838)
caveat: Napoleon's exact words and the role of Josephine come from Jenner's admiring biographer and cannot be confirmed.
